part.text:
Fixed. The problem was in `src/db.c`, where the no-touch logic checked only `server.current_client->cmd` to decide whether a lookup was performed by TOUCH. Inside a script, `server.current_client` is still the client running EVAL/FCALL, so a script-invoked `TOUCH` was wrongly treated as a regular read and had `LOOKUP_NOTOUCH` applied.

Changes (src/db.c):
- Added `currentCommandIsTouch()` (src/db.c:415), which checks both `server.current_client->cmd` and `server.executing_client->cmd` (the client tracking the command actually running, including script/module clients), comparing against `touchCommand`.
- Used it in `dbCtrlLookupClientBlocksTouch` (src/db.c:429) and in the no-touch check in `lookupKeyReadWithFlags` (src/db.c:1218) so script TOUCH still updates LRU/LFU while script reads still respect no-touch.

Verified:
- Manual repro from the issue now works: `eval "redis.call('touch', KEYS[1])" 1 foo` resets `object idletime` in no-touch mode; plain reads in no-touch mode still don't touch.
- Test suites pass: `unit/introspection-2`, `unit/scripting`, `unit/keyspace`, `unit/expire`, `unit/functions`.
